messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High queue depth and increased 5xxs for /v1/generate (hosted). Trigger: autoscale-queue-depth > 12000 for 3m, error-rate >= 8%

maria.k: I'm oncall. joining. any immediate customer-visible impact?

noah.p: Customers seeing timeouts and 503s. Alerts show 30% 5xx on the hosted API, median latency spiked from 120ms -> 2.1s. Queue depth metric at 18.5k. Paging Tier: P1.

maria.k: ack. can someone post the kube HPA and pool status?

noah.p: quick dump:
```
# k8s: autoscaler HPA
namespace=redwood-serving
autoscalers: model-worker-hpa
desiredReplicas: 18 -> 36 (scale up in progress)
currentReplicas: 18
maxReplicas: 50
events: Scale up triggered at 1854320840, cooldown 30s
```

noah.p: GPU pools: 
```
gpu-pool-a: nodes=40 used=40 free=0
gpu-pool-b: nodes=20 used=18 free=2 (region-b)
pending_pods: 420 pending due to scheduling/warmup
```

li.z: looking at logs. model load times shot up because new warmup path hit disk. avg model-warmup=85s for our 13B variant (should be ~12s for warm cached). KV cache misses high.

sam.dev: PromQL snippets:
```
rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",status=500}[1m])
queue_depth = sum(queue_length{pool!=""})
```
queue_depth -> 18500 at 1854320900.

maria.k: hypothesis 1: GPU pool saturation + slow model warmup (cold start) causing backlog. hypothesis 2: aggressive batching creating oversized batches leading to memory pressure and OOMs on some pods triggering restarts. we need evidence.

noah.p: evidence for h2: kube events show OOMKilled on 3 pods in last 10m. logs: 
```
2026-03-15T12:01:05Z model-worker-27 OOMKilled
2026-03-15T12:02:12Z model-worker-29 restart reason: OOMKilled
```

li.z: evidence for h1: node allocatable GPU reported full at 12:00, and model-load latency for 13B spiked to 80-120s because files were being fetched from remote blobstore (cold cache).

eng-platform: note: autoscaler is k8s-based but we have a warmup-controller disabled for this pool (testing). That's probably why warmup isn't pre-warming.

maria.k: immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) route new traffic to smaller 7B model variant via routing policy fallback, 2) reduce per-request max_tokens to lower batch sizes temporarily, 3) bump burst capacity to dedicated spare nodes if available (requesting eng-platform).

eng-platform: bump approved: allocating 8 spare GPUs from reserved pool to gpu-pool-b now (ETA ~120s for scheduling). Also enabling warmup-controller for pool-b.

noah.p: applied routing override to send non-SLA traffic to 7B fallback: 
```
POST /_admin/routing/override
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "fallback_model":"redwood-7b-fallback", "selector":"customer_tier!=enterprise" }
```

cs-ops: sending CS ping — we have ~14 customers with elevated errors. Tracking billing-sensitive accounts: acct-233, acct-882. Will email status page.

maria.k: timeline notes (in-thread):
- T0(1854320800): slight latency uptick detected by anomaly detector
- T+2m(1854320920): queue_depth > 12k, error rate rising
- T+5m(1854321100): OOMKilled events start appearing on model-worker pods
- T+8m(1854321380): autoscaler triggered scale-up but nodes were full -> pending pods grow
- T+12m(1854321520): routing override -> fallback to 7B

maria.k: collecting logs -> uploading to s3://redwood-incident-logs/1854321000/ (links below once uploaded)

li.z: uploading key artifacts: cpu/gpu metrics, kube events, model-warmup traces, batch sizes, request traces. small snippets: 
```
# model warmup trace
2026-03-15T12:00:48 load-start model=13B path=gs://models/13b-q4
2026-03-15T12:02:13 load-complete duration=85s
```

sam.dev: quick check on Batching: avg_batch_size jumped from 6->18 for the high-cost route. Batching window auto-expanded while queue deep. That increases memory per request.

maria.k: mitigation status: routing override applied, reserved GPUs allocated, warmup-controller enabled. Error rate dropped to 6% and queue_depth trending down to 6.2k. Need to stabilize and track for 30m.

noah.p: starting RCA doc draft in the incident channel: collecting hypotheses to track: 
- H1: Warmup disabled + cold model loads from blobstore -> slow node readiness -> queue backlog
- H2: Autoscaler scale-up latency vs pod warmup time -> scaling too slow relative to request arrival
- H3: Large dynamic batches during backlog -> OOMs -> pod churn -> further reduced capacity

li.z: I'll attach warmup traces and heap profiles. Owner: li.z for warmup investigation.

maria.k: handing off to Li for next 2hrs, I'm switching to support other pages. key open actions: 
- eng-platform: confirm warmup-controller config persisted for pool-b (owner: @eng-platform)
- sam.dev: collect batch-size distributions per route and propose throttle config (owner: sam.dev)
- noah.p: scrub OOM pod logs and correlate with batch sizes (owner: noah.p)
- cs-ops: customer communications (owner: cs-ops)

maria.k: summary for handoff: impact reduced, fallback in place, reserved capacity added, logs uploaded, RCA hypotheses recorded. handing off at 1854322100 to li.z.

li.z: taking over. thanks @maria.k. current snapshot: queue_depth=6200, 5xx=4.8%, pending_pods=110. I'll drive post-incident RCA and action list. planning immediate follow-ups: prewarm workflow, lower autoscaler cooldowns, guardrails on max_batch_size.

cs-ops: status page updated and customers notified. will attach customer impact spreadsheet to the RCA.

noah.p: adding a short-term tweak: cap batch_window_ms to 60ms for high-memory routes. rolling now.

li.z: logs and artifacts link: s3://redwood-incident-logs/1854321000/artifacts.tar.gz

eng-platform: confirmed warmup-controller enabled and persisted. Also made a change to reduce HPA scaleDownStabilization to 30s and scaleUp to 15s (temp).

li.z: I'll open PRs for: 1) prewarm enabled by default for our high-traffic pools, 2) add a warmup healthcheck metric to influence autoscaler decisions, 3) autoscaler tuning (minReplicaFloor). Owners will be listed in the RCA doc.

maria.k: thanks team. leaving notes in Ops-runbook and passing to postmortem. cc @cs-ops for follow up coms.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated (customer impact reduced). Incident channel created for RCA: #incident-1854321000
